https://english.radio.cz/outgoing-ambass.text: CS DE EN ES FR РУ УК Outgoing ambassador to Egypt Jukl to head Czech Centres, Macinka announces Facebook Twitter Outgoing Czech Ambassador to Egypt Ivan Jukl will become Director General of the Czech Centres from August, Foreign Minister Petr Macinka (Motorists) announced at a press conference on the future of the organisation today. Jukl will replace Jitka Pánek Jurková, whom Macinka dismissed with effect from today. The minister also said the Foreign Ministry does not plan to close any Czech Centres and instead sees potential to expand the network, for example through cooperation with Czech expatriate associations. The Czech Centres are the Czech Republic's public diplomacy institute, established by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Their main mission is to promote the country's reputation abroad and strengthen cultural relations with other countries. The organisation currently operates 26 branches across four continents. https://telex.hu/after/2026/08/21/padre-.text: Menü Kereső Amikor a pápa beköszön egy technóbuliba, tudod, hogy valami nagyon furcsa történik After Fotó: Soós Bertalan / Budapest Park Nagy Nikoletta Padre Guilherme augusztus 20-án elég nagy hátrányból indult Budapesten, alighanem az egyik legnehezebb koncertidőpontot kapta. A Budapest Parkban este fél kilenckor kezdett, miközben odakint hőségriadó volt, a város másik felén pedig már mindenki a tűzijátékot és a Parlamentre vetített fényfestést várta. Ennek ellenére meglepően sokan döntöttek úgy, hogy az államalapítás ünnepét inkább a Padre társaságában töltik. A Parkban így is szép tömeg gyűlt össze, annak ellenére, hogy Padre Guilherme finoman szólva sem a legerősebb szettjét adta le a magyar közönségnek. Ha valaki most hall először Padre Guilherme-ről, annak talán meglepő lehet, hogy valaki pap is, meg DJ is. Padre viszont főleg ennek köszönheti a hírnevét, ahogy a techno és house zenét ötvözi a vallásos dallamokkal. Csodaszép helyeken játszik ( a kassai katedrálisnál adott szettjével például tele volt a közösségi média), és paphoz képest igazán sajátos eszközökkel hirdeti az igét. Ja igen, és még azt is elérte, hogy a pápa videóüzenetben köszönjön be a bulizó közönségnek, amit azóta minden buliján meg is mutat. A portugál Guilherme Peixoto, azaz Padre Guilherme olyan életutat járt be, amiből Netflix-dokumentumfilmnek kellene készülnie: 1999 óta katolikus pap, katonai lelkészként afganisztáni és koszovói missziókban is szolgált. 2010-ben még Afganisztánban kezdett el DJ-zni, a katonáknak szervezett közösségi programokat és zenei esteket. Hazatérése után DJ-órákat vett, majd a zenével kezdetben a saját plébániájának próbált segíteni. Rendezvényeket szervezett, amelyek bevételével az egyházközségét támogatta. Aztán jött a koronavírus-járvány, a templomok bezártak a nagyközönség előtt, Padre pedig a netre költözött. Hetente DJ-szetteket kezdett streamelni, amikben már a vallási és népzenei dalokat az elektronikus zenével keverte. A technó felé fokozatosan eltolódó szettjei pedig egyre nagyobb közönségre találtak. Az igazi áttörést 2023 hozta meg neki, amikor a lisszaboni Ifjúsági Világtalálkozón először játszott rengeteg ember előtt élőben. A fellépésről készült videók bejárták a közösségi médiát, Padre Guilherme karrierje pedig kilőtt: innentől nem egy portugál pap volt, aki mellékesen DJ-zik is, hanem egy katolikus DJ, aki a zenéjén keresztül próbálja megkeresni a kapcsolatot a közönséggel. Padre alapvetően a techno, a melodic techno és a house határmezsgyéjén mozog – általában, a Budapest Parkban azért ezt kevésbé láthattuk, valamiért ide inkább a lakossági tuctuccal készült, és nem az igazán jó, veretős techno dalaival. A szett elképesztően jól indult, az első és második számmal Padre megadta a felütést az estének, de aztán valamiért eldurrogtatta az összes feldolgozást, amit egyébként általában elszórva szokott mutogatni több bulin keresztül. A mélypont kétségtelenül az volt, amikor felcsendült a Scatman – ekkor azért elmorzsoltam egy könnycseppet, visszagondolva azokra a szettjeire, amikből egymás után shazamoztam ki a jobbnál jobb technószámokat. Padréra ugyanis nem a Super Mario, a Freed From Desire, a Crazy vagy a Avicii-számok felturbózott változataiért jár az ember (mondjuk Aviciiért soha semmilyen körülmények között nem fogok senkire haragudni, azt elnézem), hanem minőségi melodic technóért: nála hallottam például először a KREAM-től az Arrivalt vagy a The Techno Code-ot Enrico Sangiulianótól – igaz, utóbbi a mostani szettbe is belefért. A Hope Touron, aminek a parkos esemény is az egyik állomása volt, viszont arányaiban túl sok volt a technósított pop, és kevés az igazi tuctuc. A közönségnek viszont jól láthatóan nagyon bejöttek ezek a dalok is, úgyhogy lehet, hogy csak én vagyok túl válogatós. Fotó: Soós Bertalan / Budapest Park Azt nem lehet mondani, hogy a buli rossz volt, amikor sikerült elengednem az elvárásaimat, én is nagyon jól éreztem magam, és volt néhány igazán emlékezetes része is az estének – Padre például lejátszotta a Queen Don't Stop Me Now című dalát is, ami bárki mástól csak egy kis retró kitekintés lett volna, egy katolikus paptól viszont állásfoglalás az elfogadás mellett. Padre Guilherme összes szettje erre épül egyébként: az összefogásra, a békére, a szeretetre és a pápa is erről beszélt a közönségnek a beköszönőjében, amit először pont a kassai bulin láthattak a nézők. XIV. Leót többször „színpadra hívta” Guilherme, a pápa egy másik beszédében emberi kapcsolatokról, barátságról, békéről és a gyűlöletbeszéd végéről beszélt. Nem ez volt az első alkalom egyébként, hogy Peixoto elnyerte egy pápa támogatását, Padre 2019-ben személyesen is találkozott Ferenc pápával. Padréból egyébként is süt az elfogadás, a kedvesség és az, hogy a zene szeretetén keresztül próbálja meg átadni a saját hitét a közönségének. Én, mint óriási ateista, emögé száz százalékosan be tudok állni, és az ilyen bulikon teljes békében együtt tud lépegetni az, aki vallásos, és mélyen átérzi Padre technósított katolikus dalait, és az, aki csak arra kíváncsi, hogyan tekeri egy katolikus pap a DJ-pultot. Az este egyik legemlékezetesebb pillanata pedig kétségkívül az volt, amikor Padre világhírű We Want Peace című számánál az első refrén után egyszer csak egy óriási lökéssel feltámadt a szél – a véletlen időzítés annyira jól sikerült, hogy ettől még az is átszellemült egy kicsit, akinek köze sincs a valláshoz. Ezen a ponton érdemes megemlékezni a Budapest Park fénytechnikájáról is, mert vérprofi volt, és rengeteget tett hozzá a buli hangulatához – még Padre kicsit esetlen galambanimációja is jól mutatott a színpadon a tökéletesen időzített fényjáték mellett, de egyébként a portugál pap is készült brutális látványelemekkel, többször úgy érezte magát az ember a bulin, mintha nem is a Parkban, hanem egy templomban vagy katedrálisban lenne. Padre aztán búcsúszámként húzott egy váratlant, és augusztus 20. alkalmából lejátszotta nekünk a Nélküled turbósított változatát – ezen a ponton látható volt a közönség döbbenete, láthatóan senki nem szólt szegény Padrénak, hogy itthon milyen felhangja van ennek a dalnak. Az igyekezetet viszont mindenképp díjazta mindenki, és énekelték is a volt kormánypárt nemhivatalos indulóját. Nem tudom, Padre Guilherme tisztában volt-e vele, hogy augusztus 20-án a Nélküledet Budapesten lejátszani nagyjából olyan, mintha valaki egy aknamezőn próbálna táncolni, de legalább bátran vállalta a kockázatot. A közönség pedig meglepően könnyen megbocsátotta neki. Valahogy egyébként még a Nélküled is belefért abba, amiért Padre Guilherme igazán működik. Nem azért, mert minden száma jó, és még csak nem is azért, mert minden szettje kifogástalan, hanem azért, mert van valami meglepően szerethető abban, ahogy egy katolikus pap több ezer ember előtt próbálja ugyanazt mondani, amit a templomban is: ne gyűlöljük egymást, béküljünk ki, és próbáljunk meg egy kicsit jobban szeretni. Ezt pedig augusztus 20-án, egy hőségriadóval, tűzijátékkal és Nélküleddel súlyosbított este közepén is nagyon jó volt hallani. Kövess minket Facebookon is! Követem! Friss az Afteren

https://www.howtogeek.com/3d-printing-yo.text: By Tim Brookes Published Aug 12, 2026, 7:00 AM EDT Tim has been covering technology for almost 20 years, in that time spanning a broad range of topics from security to product reviews. He is especially focused on the Apple ecosystem, productivity, and consumer advice. Over the years Tim has written thousands of articles, reviews, and round-ups in addition to producing video content and original photography. A graduate of journalism, he found his footing as a freelancer with a laptop and loves how he is able to work from practically anywhere. Now a Senior Editor for iPhone, Mac, and Smart Home at How-To Geek , Tim still loves to write. He can also be found crafting round-ups and productivity posts for the Zapier blog . Earlier in his career Tim spent nearly a decade as a writer and eventually Apple section editor for MakeUseOf . Tim currently lives in Brisbane, Australia. Outside of work he loves to hike and work out, play video games, and spend quality time with his wonderful partner and two cats Inka and Roger. Sign in to your How-To Geek account Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google News Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap A lot of 3D printing video content boils down to fairly simple printer reviews that often draw very similar conclusions. While being clued in on the latest printers is all well and good, there’s a lot more to the hobby than that. Today I’m going to highlight six of my favorite 3D printing-focused YouTube channels. CNCKitchen More than just videos German YouTuber Stefan, better known as CNCKitchen, runs arguably one of the better-known YouTube channels with a focus on 3D printing. This is one of the first channels I really latched onto when I became interested in the hobby, with professional production, a friendly presenter style, and a varied catalog of videos to work your way through. Stefan posts once per month (sometimes more), which includes 3D printer reviews, technique guides, and highlights for whatever he’s been up to. He has also developed a fair number of personal projects, like free tool BumpMesh which adds textures to 3D prints and a world-first insert extractor for removing hardware from existing 3D prints. I’m also a big fan of his research, which clearly requires a lot of time and work. He has tested various methods of “annealing” 3D prints in order to make them stronger like casting models in plaster , plus he blended cow manure into PLA and explored the concept of printing with it. Zack Freedman 3D printing royalty Zack Freedman is the mind behind Gridfinity, arguably 3D printing’s most successful open-source project to date. This grid-based modular storage system combines base plates with bins to keep desktops, drawers, and everything else organized. When he’s not designing new models, Zack is running a YouTube channel to showcase his latest work and insight into what makes projects tick. His videos focus a lot on what he’s making, techniques like copying parts in modeling software, weird filament types, and 3D printing with unorthodox materials like chocolate . Not every video Zack puts out concerns 3D printing, with a dash of smart home, PC building, and electronics projects thrown in for good measure. He’s also made an interesting video about the homemade contraption that he wears on his face, which many commenters mistake for Google Glass. ModBot 3D printing hardware and beyond ModBot is a channel that mainly focuses on 3D printing hardware and filament. That means lots of reviews, not just of printers but also modifications and add-ons for printer systems like ELEGOO’s CANVAS for the Centauri Carbon and aftermarket chamber heaters . Filament also gets a fair amount of airtime, particularly less common flexible materials like foaming TPU (which can be really challenging to print with ), glass fiber TPU , and PEBA . If you’re interested in improving your 3D printed experience by looking beyond the wall of what manufacturers like Bambu Lab have put up, ModBot is worth a watch. Maker’s Muse Don’t try this at home Maker’s Muse is all about empowering creativity through technology, which explains the slightly offbeat approach to content you’ll find on the channel. A lot of the focus is on testing out weird techniques and hacks, then dispelling any myths that surround them. A lot of these are things you really wouldn’t want to do at home for fear of endangering you or your printer, which makes them all the more entertaining to watch. The channel has also started a 3D printing mastery series, in which concepts like layer height and infill patterns and density are explained for all ability levels. There are also a good number of software tips, including slicer settings and CAD concepts to be aware of. Beyond this, the channel leans into some 3D printing-adjacent topics like UV printing. Slant3D Life on the print farm Slant3D is the YouTube channel of the print farm of the same name. The channel uploads a weekly podcast detailing what they’re up to and what’s going on in the world of 3D printing, along with useful guides, advice, tips, and explainers. The channel often takes on challenges, like improving 3D printed LEGO or 3D printing a part that was previously believed to be impossible . They’ve also been known to “steal” designs and improve them for other creators (and YouTube views, obviously). In addition to polished and illuminating content, Slant3D provides some insight into a side of 3D printing that many home enthusiasts don’t see: what it’s like running a large manufacturing operation that depends on printers to stay in business. Proper Printing Let him cook Proper Printing is the YouTube channel of Jón Schone, a creator who is affiliated with Prusa and who moved to Prague in order to take the company up on their collaborative offer. His videos can mostly be described as him building weird and wonderful things. These “slice of life” videos usually involve Jón introducing a concept, breathing life into it, and then documenting how it all pans out along the way. There are some really bonkers ideas here, including using a grill plate as a print bed for a 3D printer, pushing a Bambu Lab X1C to its limit by printing PEEK at 420ºC, and 3D printing a kayak on a treadmill . https://www.dw.com/en/india-s-citizen-le.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5JZLZ The CJP has said many government schools are in need of improvement Image: Madhan Kumar/DW Advertisement The Indian activist movement dubbing itself the "Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)" shot to national prominence in May by leading weeks-long protests over a scandal involving highly competitive entrance exams. The student-led campaign put the government under intense political pressure and ended with the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan in July. Now, the CJP is taking aim at India's government schools , organizing volunteer visits to classrooms, documenting conditions and demanding accountability for problems. Launched on August 15, Independence Day in India , the campaign asks parents, students and volunteers to inspect schools and record basic facilities including toilets, drinking water, electricity, classroom furniture and school buildings. The CJP has said the findings will be used to pressure authorities to make improvements. The initial target is to audit 100 rural government schools over two months. It has also proposed giving recognition to village leaders who improve their schools. Unlike the first campaign, which was based on street protests, the school audits require a more sustained form of local activism . Volunteers are expected to work consistently at the local level, document conditions and follow up with officials, parents and communities. Students celebrated in New Delhi after the resignation of India's education minister in July Image: Raj K Raj/Hindustan Times/Sipa USA/picture alliance The organization is dealing with different layers of the Indian administration. Responsibility for government schools is divided between state governments, local administrations and elected village bodies. The CJP is therefore set to tackle different rules and political interests across the country. India has over a million government schools, according to Education Ministry data. They make up nearly 70% of all schools in the country but serve less than half of its 247 million schoolchildren. CJP: 'We are not afraid' That scale has given CJP a vast field for its campaign. But it has also brought a new set of challenges. The authorities are raising questions regarding rules and locations for the CJP scrutiny, as well as safeguards when children are present. The response is already varying from state to state. Some authorities have ordered their own inspections, while others have restricted access or taken police action against CJP volunteers. Authorities in Maharashtra and Rajasthan states have objected to school visits carried out without permission. In one case, a complaint by school authorities resulted in police action against CJP members after they entered the premises to conduct an audit. In Rajasthan, restrictions have been imposed on outsiders entering government schools, as well as on filming, interviews and other forms of documentation. CJP volunteers in Rajasthan have also said they were attacked while inspecting a school . "We are not afraid. We are seeking accountability from the government," said CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka. Officials say schools are not open spaces In the state of Uttar Pradesh, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has ordered officials to conduct on-the-spot checks of school facilities and directed police to register cases over what he called misleading videos about schools and colleges. India's 'Cockroach' protesters claim online censorship To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video The CJP has said such measures undermine public scrutiny. Authorities have said schools are not open spaces for unauthorized inspections, particularly when children are present. Vinita Gursahani Singh, managing trustee of We, The People campaign, which works on citizen empowerment, said the limits are set by law. "Under the Right to Information Act, any citizen can inspect schools but you need to submit an application. And that makes sense as there has to be consideration for students and teaching," Singh told DW. "All public scrutiny is legitimate. It is our job to scrutinize. But the scrutiny has to follow process. It has to be even-handed. What applies to one citizen must apply to all," she said. Can activists serve as inspectors? The CJP maintains government schools are publicly funded institutions and citizens have a legitimate right to ask how they are functioning. Its volunteers use standardized audit forms to record conditions and send their findings to the CJP, which has said it will use the material to press local administrations to respond. But critics question whether citizen activists can assume the role of inspectors. There are concerns about whether volunteers have the expertise to assess safety or infrastructure problems and how allegations posted on social media are verified. Mohandas Pai, an education advocate, supports CJP's focus on government schools but disagrees with its methods. "I like young people taking interest in school education. It's a broken system, and we need reforms," Pai told DW. But he objected to large groups entering schools and questioning headmasters and children. "You can't just barge into a school just because you think you are entitled to do it," Pai said, stressing that "children have to have a safe, secure environment." India's elementary school helping students escape poverty To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Pai said the CJP should instead send small teams with permission, collect systematic data, publish regular reports and use the evidence to pressure governments. CJP spokesperson Saurav Das rejected the argument that the campaign should rely on conventional channels, saying such approaches have failed to bring meaningful change. Responding to Pai on X, he challenged him to join the next school visit and show the volunteers how it should be done. Questions of student privacy The audit campaign has also raised questions about privacy, consent and disruption of teaching when volunteers enter schools, film inside classrooms or question students. However, Kavita Srivastava, president of the People's Union for Civil Liberties (PUCL) Rajasthan, opposes restrictions on outsiders entering schools and taking photos and videos in her state. "Activists were visiting government schools to document their condition and demand accountability. Protecting children's privacy should not be used to prevent legitimate public scrutiny of government schools," Srivastava told DW. A new role for the CJP Activist Amrita Johri said the CJP's first campaign tapped into a longstanding accountability gap in India's examination system, which cost millions of young people time and money. "The demand for accountability had popular resonance because there was no real response from the government," Johri told DW. She backed the school audit campaign, saying public scrutiny should be welcomed. "Public audits are an integral part of citizens' right to information and should be welcomed as an opportunity to fix accountability," she said. Johri added that the CJP needs to train volunteers, document problems and follow up with authorities to make the campaign effective. https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/s.text: Soldiers halt an Israeli peace activist trying to reach Palestinians facing a blockade in their dispute with settlers near Qusra in the occupied West Bank. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Soldiers halt an Israeli peace activist trying to reach Palestinians facing a blockade in their dispute with settlers near Qusra in the occupied West Bank. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images Israel ‘It’s a good start’: prominent Israelis welcome UK sanctions on illegal settlements Ed Miliband’s intervention was ‘inevitable’ after Israeli government and security failures, say former ministers and diplomats Emma Graham-Harrison in Jerusalem Wed 9 Sep 2026 13.36 EDT Last modified on Wed 9 Sep 2026 13.55 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Prominent Israelis have welcomed new UK sanctions as a necessary response to settlement expansion and spiralling violence in the occupied West Bank. The intervention was described – by the president of the Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities, a former prime minister, an ex-head of the army and former ministers and diplomats – as an “inevitable consequence” of Israeli government and security failures. “Sanctions [are being imposed] against Jewish terrorists, and not against the legitimacy of the state of Israel,” they wrote in a joint statement. “There is no basis to the [Israeli] government’s response that the decision to impose sanctions against Jewish terrorists is an expression of antisemitism.” Ed Miliband, the foreign secretary, had indicated Britain was planning new sanctions but the strength of his language and the scale of the controls he announced on Tuesday were a surprise. It was the most significant attempt in many years, from a close Israeli ally, to leverage economic power to force change in the occupied West Bank . “Israel’s government has caused a rupture in the longest-standing diplomatic convention of all: using obfuscation and plenty of ‘very concerned’ statements instead of actually doing anything,” Esther Solomon wrote in the Haaretz newspaper. The impact was multiplied when France and Canada announced plans for trade bans on settlement goods and 10 other European countries backed similar measures. Nor did any senior figure in the Trump administration, which was briefed in advance on the UK plans, criticise the measures. View image in fullscreen The Jewish settlement of Karnei Shomron, north-east of Tel Aviv. A poll suggests almost three-quarters of Jewish Israelis want to annex the occupied West Bank. Photograph: Amir Levy/Getty Images “Jerusalem had prepared for rain, but what arrived yesterday was a full-blown storm,” Itamar Eichner wrote in Yedioth Ahronoth. “Yesterday Israel was caught off guard, to the point that senior Israeli officials used the term ‘an intelligence-diplomatic failure’.” Nearly three-quarters of Jewish Israelis favour partial or total annexation of the occupied West Bank, a poll for the Jewish People Policy Institute found. All leading candidates in the upcoming election reject a Palestinian state. However, there is increasingly vocal opposition to settler violence and expansion from some members of the country’s security, political and cultural elites. They threatened legal action against their government this summer over its support for Jewish terrorism and an “ideology of ethnic cleansing” in the occupied West Bank. Prof David Harel, British-born president of the Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities, is among those who signed a statement backing the UK measures. He said the sanctions offered urgently needed support for Israelis like him, who are trying to stop attacks on Palestinians and end the occupation. “I personally would fight until my last breath against antisemitism and against anti-Israelism. For that reason, I’m against general wall-to-wall boycott, divest, sanction-style sanctions on the state of Israel,” the leading scientist told the Guardian. “But what is justified, and I do support, is being anti things that Israel is doing, and these days in particular what it is doing in the West Bank.” He said that Israelis calling for a delay until after the elections were ignoring both the escalating violence that Palestinians faced every day and the risks the occupation posed to Israel’s future. “Getting out of there [occupied Palestine], or, at least for the present, stopping these things from happening and starting to really talk about a two-state solution is not only good for the Palestinians. It’s not that we’re doing these poor people a favour. We’re doing a favour to ourselves, no less, maybe even more.” The joint statement backing the UK sanctions was also signed by former prime minister Ehud Olmert, former commander of the Israeli military Dan Halutz, former ministers Yuli Tamir and Roni Bar-On and former ambassador to Germany Yoram Ben Zeev. “This decision is precisely what the state of Israel should have received in order to remove the disgrace of Jewish terrorism from the face of the country,” they wrote. Map showing countries with sanctions on Israeli settlements Nadav Tamir, a former diplomat, also described the measures as good for Israel. “Any move to prevent annexation and ethnic cleansing of the Palestinians in the West Bank [and Gaza] is serving the long-term interests of the Zionist vision of Israel as the democratic homeland of the Jewish people,” he said. “It will help us to be more secure and moral.” The value of goods exported from occupied territories to Britain last year was only $45m (£33m) out of total $4.4bn trade in goods and services, according to Roey Fisher, head of Israel’s Foreign Trade Administration. However, plans to place sanctions on any company that finances or facilitates settlement expansion could force Israel’s main banks and insurance companies to choose between their business interests in the UK and those in occupied Palestine. Miliband has not provided details of the new measures but the move has the potential to slow or stop construction. Avraham Burg, a former speaker of the Knesset, thanked Miliband for setting a global example. “Like many Israelis and Palestinians I am grateful for the courageous moral leadership of Miliband. It’s a good beginning. Do not stop,” he said. But Israel’s foreign minister, Gideon Sa’ar, attacked Miliband for “blatant interference” in his country’s domestic affairs before a late October election. Opposition politicians suggested instead that Benjamin Netanyahu might weaponise the UK sanctions to bolster his campaign to remain prime minister. View image in fullscreen Gideon Sa’ar, Israel’s foreign minister (left), strikes a deal with his Slovenian counterpart, Tone Kajzer, in Ljubljana on Wednesday. He said the UK sanctions were ‘blatant interference’ in Israeli affairs. Photograph: Darko Bandić/AP Dahlia Scheindlin , one of Israel’s leading political analysts, said the UK move was very unlikely to affect the October election, because Israeli voters were more focused on domestic issues. “Since 7 October [2023], Israel has become much more inward-looking and provincial, and generally the attitude to the rest of the world is just that ‘they all hate us’,” Scheindlin said. “If you are a Netanyahu supporter you might take this as evidence that they are against us because of antisemitism, and if you are in the opposition camp you might take this as further evidence that the world is turning against us because of Netanyahu’s policies. But it’s hard to see how these policies change the breakdown of the electoral map.” Miliband made his speech on a day when political parties finalised their candidate lists and Haaretz had a bombshell story about security warnings delivered to Netanyahu – and apparently ignored – before the 7 October attacks. Fourteen Israeli human rights organisations welcomed the sanctions. “This is an important and necessary first step to meet states’ legal obligation,” said the statement from groups including B’Tselem, Physicians for Human Rights Israel and Breaking the Silence. “We urge the international community to take further concrete measures to ensure that its relations with Israel no longer enable Israel’s settlement enterprise, forced displacement and ethnic cleansing in the occupied West Bank, or its broader assault on Palestinian human rights across all territories under its control.” Explore more on these topics Israel Palestine West Bank Middle East and north Africa Ed Miliband Foreign policy Israel-Gaza war news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed US news US politics Midterms 2026 World Climate crisis Middle East Ukraine US immigration Soccer Business Environment Tech Science Newsletters The Filter Wellness

Moscow is also considering expanding its use of conventional ballistic missiles against infrastructure across Ukraine, according to Bloomberg, which cited four sources familiar with the thinking inside the Russian leadership. The sources said attempts to revive negotiations had effectively collapsed, leaving the two sides back at square one. Russia increasingly regards Ukrainian attacks as attacks by NATO itself, given the weapons, intelligence and other support provided to Kyiv by alliance members. “The current stage of hostilities isn’t the peak of military escalation,” the sources said. The assessment underscores the growing risk that Russia could intensify its campaign against Ukrainian cities and critical infrastructure just as diplomatic efforts involving Washington face mounting obstacles. Read more related news: UK on red alert: Brits told to prepare for an attack as Russian war plans pushed forward Putin is planning an imminent test on N ATO which forces CIA chief to rush to Moscow UK intelligence warns Kremlin is ‘preparing something’ as security source warns Burnham will be tested UK is in Russia’s crosshairs as Putin warns he will attack British military sites Latvian President Edgars Rinkēvičs said on June 6 that NATO needed to remain prepared for worst-case scenarios, describing Russia as dangerous and unpredictable and warning that its next move was difficult to anticipate . The concern extends beyond Ukraine. NATO’s eastern members, particularly the Baltic states, have increasingly been preparing for the possibility that the conflict could spill over into their territory. Drones have repeatedly entered the airspace of countries including Romania and Poland, while Moldova has also faced security concerns linked to the war. Russia has simultaneously stepped up efforts to prepare its population for a potential confrontation with NATO by 2030, while European governments have reported an increase in Russian hybrid activity and cyberattacks. According to Bloomberg’s sources, President Vladimir Putin is unlikely to abandon the war because of European sanctions or Ukrainian attacks against Russian oil, energy and logistics infrastructure. Four people close to the Kremlin said Russia now saw few alternatives to further escalation if it was to achieve its military objectives. Moscow is nevertheless awaiting a possible diplomatic initiative from US special envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff. Russian officials hope their visit could produce new proposals, although expectations of a breakthrough remain limited. The stakes are particularly high because some Russian officials increasingly believe Putin could eventually consider the use of tactical nuclear weapons as a last resort in Ukraine. “An extreme response is viewed as possible because the only outcome worse than continuing the war for Putin would be losing it,” Bloomberg reported, while stressing that there is currently no indication Russia is preparing to use nuclear weapons . The warnings came as CIA Director John Ratcliffe travelled to Moscow on Tuesday, August 25, after flying from Riga in a US military transport aircraft. Flight-tracking data indicated that a C-17 Globemaster III arrived in Riga on Sunday, August 23, after departing from Camp Springs, Maryland, home to Andrews Air Force Base. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov initially denied knowledge of the aircraft. “We have no information about this,” Peskov said when asked about the flight, adding that Russia was not planning meetings with the US administration. Peskov subsequently said Putin and Ratcliffe had not met. The Kremlin later confirmed Ratcliffe’s visit, saying there had been “talks between the intelligence services”. Axios, citing two anonymous US officials, reported that Washington had informed Kyiv ahead of the trip that a high-level US delegation was travelling to Moscow and had asked Ukraine not to launch strikes on the Russian capital. The purpose of Ratcliffe’s visit remains unclear. Analysts have suggested that talks with Russian intelligence officials could have focused on the war in Ukraine, wider security issues or the conflict between the US and Iran. On the same day as Ratcliffe’s visit, Putin signed three undisclosed decrees. Documents numbered 605, 606 and 607 were signed but not published, leaving their contents unknown. US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that Ratcliffe’s trip could produce results as Washington continued efforts to bring the war to an end. “We would like to see the Ukraine war end,” Trump said, adding that his administration was “working very hard to get that war ended.” “Something may come out of it,” he continued. For Kyiv, the prospect of renewed Russian escalation comes at a particularly sensitive moment, with diplomacy stalled but Washington still seeking a route towards a settlement. The Kremlin’s reported conclusion that negotiations have reached a dead end suggests the coming weeks could instead be defined by an intensification of military pressure, raising the risks for Ukraine and for NATO states along Russia’s western flank.
